predecessors.name: Oghuz Yabgu State
predecessors.text: the lower Syr Darya around Cend, left by Seljuk's clan when it broke with the Oghuz Yabghu

successors.name: Great Seljuk Empire
successors.text: the Seljuk state after Dandanaqan (23 May 1040), with Khorasan won from the Ghaznavids

capitals.name: Cend (Jand), on the lower Syr Darya

ledger.x: 985: Seljuk, leader of his clan, breaks with the Oghuz Yabghu and settles on the lower Syr Darya, with his seat at Cend.
1035: the Seljuks defeat the Ghaznavids at Nasa.
1035: Mas'ud cedes three Khorasan cities to the Seljuks.
1037: Tughril and Chaghri take Merv and Nishapur.
1037: the old seat on the Syr Darya is left behind.
1039: the fight for Khorasan passes to the Great Seljuk row.
1039: the Seljuk dynasty's own row ends and the Great Seljuk Empire follows.

wars.name: Seljuk-Ghaznavid struggle for Khorasan (to Dandanaqan)
wars.outcome: Seljuk victories at Nasa (1035), then Merv and Nishapur (1037-1038); the Ghaznavids lose Khorasan at Dandanaqan on 23 May 1040 (great-seljuk-empire dossier).

certainty.note: A tribal range on the Syr Darya and then a few Khorasan cities held by a nomadic army: no frontier is fixed on any page.
